speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to help narrow this down, how long has this rash been present and does it appear in a specific pattern or shape?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pityriasis rosea (herald patch followed by trunk/extremity lesions, though bilateral upper extremity predominance is atypical; consider contact dermatitis or scabies pending history of others in household or occupational exposure).

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of rash, full body skin exam photos.
